title: Gunman Kills Six in Krakow's Main Market Square; Police Shoot Suspect
dek: A 25-year-old Polish man opened fire from a vehicle on a crowded square on Saturday afternoon, police said. Three more bodies were later found at his home, and officials are investigating his ideology.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial-style view of Kraków's Main Market Square with the St. Mary's Basilica and historic buildings

keyPoints: Six people were killed and more than a dozen injured when a gunman fired on the Main Market Square in Krakow around 3:30 p.m. local time on Saturday.
Police shot the suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, at the scene; he is in serious condition and undergoing surgery.
Three bodies were found at the suspect's home, which authorities are still searching.
Poland's interior minister said authorities are evaluating reports that the attacker was fixated on far-right ideologies.
body:
Six people were killed and at least 15 were injured on Saturday when a gunman opened fire in the Main Market Square of Krakow, one of Poland's best-known tourist and cultural centers, according to officials.

## What authorities have said

Police said the shots were fired from a vehicle moving through the square shortly after 3:30 p.m. local time. Officers returned fire within minutes of receiving reports of the attack. The attacker, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, was shot by police at the scene and taken to hospital, where he is undergoing surgery in serious condition, according to Poland's interior minister and local officials.

Police spokespeople said the suspect wore military-style clothing and used a military-type long gun. They also reported finding additional weapons and ammunition in his car.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that three bodies were later found at the suspect's home. He said they appeared to be members of the suspect's close family, and that authorities were searching the house for weapons and checking whether the car could pose a further threat.

## Casualties

The head of Poland's national police, Marek Boron, said that three of the dead were Polish citizens and that a British citizen was among the six killed. Two of the dead had not been identified at the time of his briefing. NBC News, citing police, reported that four women and two men were killed. Officials have not yet released a full, confirmed list of names.

Among the injured are two police officers who were shot during the confrontation; both have undergone surgery. Officials said five foreign nationals were also among those being treated.

## Motive under review

Poland's interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said authorities were evaluating reports that the attacker was fixated on far-right political ideologies. Tusk said he was confident that authorities would quickly identify and detain any possible supporters of the suspect. No further motive has been confirmed, and officials have not released the suspect's name.

## Reaction and what comes next

The Krakow city government announced a mourning period through November 11. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the United Kingdom stood in solidarity with Poland.

Investigators are expected to release more information about the attacker, his associates and the weapons used as the day goes on. Meridian will update this story if officials confirm names, a motive or a revised casualty count.
